ai.title: Switch read-only-commander to Sonnet 4.5
ai.summary: The read-only-commander agent definition in .agents/read-only-commander.ts now uses anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5 instead of openai/gpt-5-chat. This change leverages prompt caching for cost efficiency and simplifies reasoning options. The agent's system prompt inheritance and instruction structure were also updated to align with the new model's capabilities.

eli5.text: An internal helper the system uses to investigate and summarize the codebase has quietly switched from OpenAI's GPT-5-chat to Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 4.5. If you noticed this agent answering questions, you'd see it now pulls in a broader set of project context by default and can be run alongside other specialist agents at the same time, rather than being a separate side tool. Because the change is under the hood for staff and internal builders, everyday users won't see any different behavior unless someone on your team points this agent at a new task that now finishes a bit faster and cheaper thanks to the new model's cost-saving setup.

ai.title: Base2 Orchestrator Refactor and GPT-5-High Cleanup
ai.summary: Refactored `base2` to use a new orchestrator pattern with `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5`, replacing the old factory setup. Removed legacy `gpt-5-high` agent definitions (`base2-gpt-5-high`, `editor-gpt-5-high`, `reviewer-gpt-5-high`, `thinker-gpt-5-high`) and associated planner factories. Updated system prompts and tool configurations in `.agents/base2/base2.ts` to support the new spawnable agents list.

eli5.text: The main helper that runs your coding tasks was rebuilt to coordinate work in a new way, and it now uses an upgraded model to do so. As part of the same update, several older variants that relied on a different provider were removed, so only the new setup remains active. If you were watching the internals, you would see the old coordinating files gone and the new one in place; from a user standpoint, nothing you directly start has changed today, but the system behind it now runs on the newer configuration.

ai.title: Benchify integration and batch strreplace
ai.summary: Added `benchify` dependency and `BENCHIFY_API_KEY` to enable AI-assisted code transformations. Implemented `batch-str-replace.ts` to defer and batch `str_replace` tool calls using a two-phase execution strategy in `stream-parser.ts`, improving handling of multiple edits. Updated `process-str-replace.ts` to strictly track successful replacements and return errors if none occur. Adjusted `npm-app` diff line counting to exclude metadata lines.

eli5.text: The assistant now groups together many small text-editing requests to a file and applies them all at once, instead of editing each one individually, which makes large multi-edit changes faster and less likely to fail partway through. When several edits are bundled, an AI helper can review and apply them as a set, and if an edit can't find what it's looking for in the file, the system returns a clear error instead of silently doing nothing. You'd notice this as smoother, more reliable edits when the assistant rewrites chunks of code, especially when files end up with no net changes (an error is now explicitly returned instead of a vague 'no change' message). It's already live today.

ai.title: OpenRouter wrapper integration with schema updates for reasoning
ai.summary: Added OpenRouter API wrapper implementation and updated database schema to support reasoning tokens and agent IDs. Migration `0030_closed_union_jack.sql` modifies the `message` table by making `client_id`, `client_request_id`, and `request` nullable, dropping defaults for `cache_creation_input_tokens`, and adding `agent_id`, `reasoning_text`, and `reasoning_tokens` columns. New files include `web/src/llm-api/openrouter.ts` for the API client, `scripts/fat-sdk-openrouter-example.ts` for usage examples, and updated types in `web/src/llm-api/type/openrouter.ts`. The changes span core database migrations, web API routes, and shared type definitions to enable OpenRouter model access with extended metadata tracking.

eli5.text: The system now lets the assistant use a new external model provider, so it can access models that weren't available before (and this is live as of the snapshot dated 2025-10-06). When the assistant answers you, it can also save extra details about how it thought through the answer, including the actual reasoning text and how many reasoning tokens it used. If you look at conversation records, you'd see new information stored alongside each message showing which assistant agent produced it and what kind of internal reasoning happened, even for messages where some previously-required reference fields are now allowed to be missing.

ai.title: Version 1.0.501 release bump for the codebuff npm package
ai.summary: The codebuff npm package version is bumped from 1.0.500 to 1.0.501 in npm-app/release/package.json as part of a release-bump commit. No source code, feature, or schema changes accompany this version increment; it reflects a packaging-only step. This follows earlier work on OpenRouter integration, base2 orchestrator refactor, and Benchify batch str-replace tooling that shipped in the prior day's commits.
ai.evidence: The diff shows a single one-line version bump in npm-app/release/package.json from 1.0.500 to 1.0.501, reflecting a release-bump commit with no source code changes.

eli5.text: This release delivers major improvements to how AI coding agents plan and execute complex tasks, with new model updates and smarter automation throughout. The biggest addition is a new orchestrator agent system that breaks down complicated coding projects into smaller steps, assigning specialized sub-agents to planning, research, editing, and review work, all powered by the latest Claude Sonnet 4.5 and other advanced models. Users can now benefit from automatic retries when tracking message costs, preventing billing errors during temporary service issues, plus a new batch string replacement feature that handles multiple file edits more reliably. The release also introduces Benchify integration for AI-assisted code transformations, improves directory and file path resolution for smoother operation across different environments, and adds a shorter 'cb' command as an alternative to typing 'codebuff' for quicker terminal access. Upgrading means more stable, efficient, and capable coding assistance with fewer errors, better cost tracking, and support for the latest AI models right out of the box.

ai.title: Add debug log to applyBenchifyIfNeeded
ai.summary: Added `logger.debug` call to `applyBenchifyIfNeeded` in `backend/src/tools/batch-str-replace.ts`. Logs `options` and `batchContext` before applying Benchify results. Internal change only.

eli5.text: Behind the scenes, the team added a small note to the system's internal records. When the assistant works on rewriting pieces of code, it now quietly saves extra details about what it’s about to change. This doesn’ change how anything works for you, but it helps the people who build and fix the system understand what happened if something goes wrong later.

ai.title: Add debug logs to batch-str-replace Benchify flow
ai.summary: Added three `logger.debug` calls in `backend/src/tools/batch-str-replace.ts` to trace the Benchify application pipeline. Logs capture `batchContext` state, `filteredChanges`, and `benchifyResult` at entry, pre-call, and post-response stages. Internal change; no user-facing behavior or API surface modified.

eli5.text: This is behind-the-scenes housekeeping for the assistant's text-replacement feature. Developers added a few diagnostic messages that quietly log what's happening at three moments, when the step starts, right before it talks to the Benchify service, and after it gets a reply, so they can later troubleshoot problems. You wouldn't see these messages in normal use since they only appear in internal logs, and nothing about how the feature works for you has changed.

ai.summary: Added debug logging to `executeBatchStrReplaces` and `applyBenchifyIfNeeded` in `backend/src/tools/batch-str-replace.ts`. Logs track deferred replacement counts, path grouping, operation completion, and intended change details to aid debugging. No functional changes or user-facing behavior modifications.

eli5.text: The team added more detailed tracking messages to the system's batch text-replacement tool so developers can better diagnose issues when processing multiple document edits at once. These new log entries show how many pending changes are batched, which files are being grouped, and the status of each operation without altering any actual functionality. If you were to inspect the system's diagnostic output, you'd now see additional, more granular messages about the internal steps taken during batch processing, such as grouping changes by file and confirming completion of each grouped operation.

ai.title: Full tool list for inherited system prompt agents
ai.summary: Refactored backend/src/tools/prompts.ts to export fullToolList function, generating complete tool descriptions. backend/src/templates/strings.ts now conditionally uses fullToolList instead of getShortToolInstructions when agentTemplate.inheritParentSystemPrompt is true. Ensures spawned agents with inherited prompts receive full tool context. Internal backend logic change affecting agent prompt construction.

eli5.text: Agents that inherit a parent system prompt now receive the complete list of available tools in their instructions, instead of just a short summary. Previously, spawned agents with the inherited prompt setting got only abbreviated tool guidance; now they get the full tool descriptions, so they have complete context from the start. This affects backend agent prompt construction and is live for any spawned agent where inheriting the parent system prompt is enabled.

ai.title: Clarify spawnable agents list
ai.summary: Updated agent spawn prompts to explicitly restrict spawnable agents to the listed types. `backend/src/templates/prompts.ts` now states that only the listed agents are available, ignoring prior references. `.agents/base2/base2.ts` workflow step updated to spawn specific researcher types in parallel.

eli5.text: The system that coordinates helper tasks now tells those helpers exactly which specialized researchers they are allowed to call for, instead of a vague reference to a generic researcher. When a coding task needs background work, it now spawns three specific researcher types, one that explores the file structure, one that searches the web, and one that reads documentation, all at the same time. The internal instructions that guide the assistant were updated on 2025-10-06 to make this restriction explicit, so anything mentioned before but not on that short list is no longer reachable. Only the two internal coordination files changed, each adding or removing just one line, and the change is live today.

ai.title: batch-str-replace reads local files
ai.summary: backend/src/tools/batch-str-replace.ts now uses requestFiles to fetch local file contents instead of relying on client-side fileContext. BatchContext maps for editedFiles and intendedChanges converted to Records. Removed unused file import and excessive debug logging.

eli5.text: The assistant now reads project files directly from your computer's local storage instead of relying on file contents sent from your browser or app. This behind-the-scenes change makes batch text replacements more reliable by fetching file data through the backend's request system, and removes unused code and extra debug logging that was cluttering the process. It affects all internal users who rely on bulk find-and-replace operations across multiple files, such as when applying formatting fixes or updating shared configuration. You probably won't notice anything different unless you're running batch edits at scale, in which case the process should complete a bit more smoothly.

eli5.text: When the assistant is working through a multi-step task, your original request will now stay visible the entire time it is working, instead of being cleared away after each step. This affects the backend agent loop that powers automated reasoning and any sub-agents it spins up to help, so they always have your full instruction in view while they run.

ai.title: Add ROADMAP.md
ai.summary: New ROADMAP.md file added to the repository root. Documents current internal engineering priorities: rebuilding npm-app with TUI/SDK, moving backend logic to SDK, and developing base2 agent. Includes a note on daily plan re-evaluation.

eli5.text: The team published their internal game plan for the next few weeks, so anyone watching the project can see what they're focusing on right now. It tells you that the engineering staff are rebuilding the command-line tool from scratch with a new visual interface, moving more of the work onto your own computer instead of a remote server, and building a smarter version of their automated programming helper that you can try out today by typing a special command. Nothing changed in how anything works yet because of this, it's just a posted schedule of where effort is being spent.

ai.title: SDK removes prompt response schema validation
ai.summary: SDK and npm-app stop enforcing PromptResponseSchema on incoming actions. Client treats prompt responses as black boxes, passing them directly to server logic without full structural validation. Only AgentOutputSchema remains validated in sdk/src/run.ts for output fields. This prevents errors from minor schema mismatches in sessionState or other non-critical fields.

eli5.text: The assistant now treats prompt responses as opaque data, skipping strict structural checks before forwarding them to the server. This affects anyone running agents through the SDK or the npm app, meaning minor schema mismatches in session state or metadata no longer cause the response to be rejected or logged as an error. If you look at the logs, you would notice fewer malformed-prompt-response error messages and more responses being passed through without validation, since only the final output schema remains checked.

ai.title: Remove spawnagentsasync tool and async agent manager
ai.summary: Removed spawn_agents_async tool definition, handler, and associated AsyncAgentManager infrastructure. Deleted superagent factory and async registration logic from run-agent-step.ts. Updates affect backend tool lists, websocket handlers, and common constants to eliminate asynchronous agent spawning support.

eli5.text: A feature that let one assistant silently spawn and coordinate multiple helper assistants in the background has been turned off and its supporting pieces deleted. You would not see a new button or option for this anywhere, any workflows or automations that depended on that background spawning will now run without it, and the assistants will only do work the direct way instead of quietly farming parts out to other assistants behind the scenes. The change is live now for anyone using the assistant, because the code that powered it is no longer part of the system.
